entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Communist Manifesto was a seminal work published in 1848 by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, born out of the European socialist movement and influenced by the Industrial Revolution. This 188-page pamphlet, initially titled \
    "The Communist Manifesto: A Contribution to the History of Materialism from 1817 to 1883\", outlined the principles of communism, predicting a future where class struggle would eventually lead to the downfall of capitalism. The Manifesto, written in collaboration with Engels, drew heavily from the German philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel's \
    \
    "Philosophy of Right\" and the French economist Pierre-Joseph Proudhon's \
    \
    \
    \
    \


    The Manifesto's impact was profound, sparking global revolutionary movements and influencing political thought for centuries to come. The manifesto's predictions of a classless society and the eventual collapse of capitalism have been both praised and criticized, with some viewing it as a prophetic vision and others as a naive utopian dream. Despite this, the Communist Manifesto remains a foundational text of modern socialism and communism, shaping the intellectual landscape of the 20th century.

    \

    The Manifesto's significance lies in its ability to galvanize a generation of workers and intellectuals, fueling the growth of socialist and communist movements across the globe. The document's influence can be seen in the Russian Revolution, the rise of Mao Zedong, and the Cuban Revolution, among other events. The Manifesto's ideas have also had a lasting impact on Marxist theory, with many scholars arguing that it represents the pinnacle of Marx's intellectual development.
